text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on May 18 in history:
1152 - Eleanor, duchess of Aquitaine, two months after her divorce from King Louis VII of France, married Henry Plantagenet (later Henry II of England) at Poitiers in France.
1291 - The Sultan of Egypt and his son Ashraf took the last Christian stronghold of Acre which broke the hold of Christians in the Holy Land.
1412 - By the treaty of Eltham, Henry IV of England allied himself with the Armagnacs with the help of the Duke of Orleans and thus abandoned the Duke of Burgundy.
1799 - Pierre Beaumarchais, French playwright, died. Famed for his two comedies "The Marriage of Figaro" and "The Barber of Seville".
1803 - Britain declared war on France after Napoleon Bonaparte continued his interference in Italy and Switzerland.
1804 - Napoleon Bonaparte was proclaimed emperor of France. He was crowned on December 2 1804.

1868 - Nicholas II, last Tsar of Russia, born. The eldest son of Tsar Alexander III, he contributed to his own unpopularity. He was overthrown by the Russian Revolution in 1917 and executed with his family the next year.

1872 - Bertrand Russell, British philosopher and mathematician, born. One of the world's outstanding philosophers, he was imprisoned twice for his views on peace and disarmament. He won the Nobel Prize for Literature in 1950.
1883 - Walter Adolph Gropius, German architect and a founder of the Bauhaus movement, born. He became professor of architecture at Harvard.

1897 - Frank Capra, U.S. screenwriter, director, producer, born in Italy. In films from 1922, he won three Oscars for "It Happened One Night", "Mr Deeds Goes to Town" and "You Can't Take It With You".
1911 - Gustav Mahler, Czech-born Austrian composer, died. He completed nine symphonies and several song-cycles notably "Das Lied von der Erde".
1920 - Pope John Paul II born as Karol Wojtyla near Krakow, Poland. He became the first non-Italian Pope in 455 years in 1978.
1944 - Allied troops, led by the Polish army, finally won the battle to evict German troops from Monte Cassino, Italy.
1944 - In the Soviet Union, the expulsion began of more than 200,000 Tatars from the Crimea. They were accused of collaboration with the Germans.
1954 - The European Convention on Human Rights came into force.
1969 - U.S spacecraft Apollo 10 was launched on a mission to rehearse for a moon landing.
1974 - India became a nuclear power when its first bomb was successfully exploded her first bomb in the Rajasthan Desert.
1980 - The eruption of Mount St Helens volcano in Washington state, began. A cloud of ash 2,500 miles long and 1,000 miles wide was created.
1980 - EEC decided to implement sanctions against Iran and a trade ban was imposed.
1980 - In Peru, the first general elections to be held since 1963 took place and resulted in a win for former President Fernando Belaunde Terry.
1990 - The two Germanys signed a monetary union treaty, the first step on the road to unification.
1993 - The Danish people voted in favour of ratifying the Maastricht Treaty in a referendum. They had rejected it in a previous vote in June 1992.
1995 - Elisha Cook Jnr, U.S. film actor, died. Best known for his role in the film "The Maltese Falcon", he also played character parts in "Shane" and "The Big Sleep".
1996 - Romano Prodi was sworn in as prime minister to head Italy's 55th government since World War Two.
